answer: A backdoor supply-chain implant attack works by an attacker exploiting vulnerabilities in the supply chain to implant malicious software into a system before it reaches the end user. This malicious software is designed to provide the attacker with unintended access to the system once it is deployed, potentially leading to further compromises or disruptions. The attack typically requires physical access to the system after it has left the manufacturer but before it is deployed at the victim's location [Source 1][Source 2].
